title: Slotmap + Warm-tier Prefetch: Operational Playbook and Design Notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational-first design for a slotmap-based KV cache combined with a lightweight warm-tier prefetcher. Goal: reduce cold-token latencies on tail requests while keeping fragmentation and memory amplification under control for multi-tenant GPUs.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: long-tail token latencies caused by KV cache misses when many short-lived keys are interleaved with hot contexts (chat sessions, short prompts). Existing slab-only designs either fragment or waste memory.
- Proposal: use a hybrid slotmap (fixed-slot index) for small/ephemeral entries and a slab pool for large/long-lived KV items. Add a warm-tier prefetcher that opportunistically promotes certain keys into the slab pool before next predicted use.
- This is an operational/playbook doc: contains heuristics, rollout guidance, metrics to watch, and runbook steps for debugging. Not a full spec of types/kernels; links to kernel-level notes included.

Design overview (concise):
1) Slotmap index (fast-path):
   - A compact, contiguous array of 64-bit entries. Each entry encodes: key fingerprint (40 bits), version tag (8 bits), and state flags (in-use, dirty, pinned).
   - Designed for O(1) single-instruction lookups (fingerprint compare + atomic load).
   - Slotmap stays in GPU L2-friendly memory layout; density tuned for ~75% occupancy.

2) Slab pool (slow-path):
   - Slabs allocated for long-lived or large KVs (e.g., > 2KB or observed > 5 hits within 30s).
   - Slabs are grouped by size classes; coalescing allowed when adjacent free slabs exist.
   - Eviction from slab pool uses a sampled LRU with epoch buckets to avoid full-list lock contention.

3) Warm-tier prefetcher:
   - Operates as an asynchronous scheduler in the serving runtime. Observes request streams and promotes keys flagged by the prefetch policy into slab pool ahead of predicted reuse.
   - Two prefetch signals: short-window recency (N hits within M seconds) and cross-request affinity (same session or same prompt template).
   - Prefetch rate is throttled by a budget per-GPU to avoid perturbing latency SLOs. Prefetches run in background CUDA streams at low priority.

4) Eviction policy (two-stage):
   - Stage A (slotmap churn): aggressive reclaim of ephemeral slots using a generational TTL and per-shard circular reclamation pointer. This keeps slotmap fragmentation low and boundaries compact.
   - Stage B (slab eviction): slab pool evictions triggered when free memory < threshold; uses sampled LRU + hotness scoring (hits/sec, last_access_age, pinned_flag). Fallback to compress/quantize slab payloads before eviction if supported.

5) Fragmentation mitigation:
   - Periodic slab rewriter: compacts active slabs into fresh larger slabs during low utilization windows (configurable per-cluster).
   - Fast coalescer: on every free operation, try buddy-style coalescing within same size class local to the shard.
   - Admission control: avoid admitting oversized ephemeral keys into slab pool; instead, keep them in slotmap with compressed payload (delta-encoding) until they demonstrate repeated hits.

Implementation notes and interactions with runtime kernels/scheduler:
- Atomic operations: slotmap reads use lock-free sequences; writes use CAS loops with short backoff. Kernel should favor single-warp operations for slot lookups to preserve occupancy.
- Background prefetch tasks submit work to a separate kernel queue with lower GPU priority. Ensure CUDA stream priorities are configured to not block tail-path generation kernels.
- KV eviction signals exported as runtime events (eviction_candidate, prefetch_started, prefetch_applied) to Console/observability pipeline. Attach token-level traces to prefetch events to measure impact.

Heuristics and thresholds (initial defaults):
- Slot size threshold: 2KB (below => slotmap candidate; above => slab candidate).
- Prefetch trigger: key seen >= 3 times in 20s OR same session sees key twice across two sequential requests.
- Prefetch budget: 5% of available device memory or X MB/GPU (configurable by instance class).
- Slab compaction window: run during 02:00-04:00 UTC for hosted clusters with low load; in Dedicated/Private this is policy-configurable.

Operational metrics to monitor (must be on dashboards):
- slotmap_hit_rate (per-shard), slab_hit_rate, overall_kv_miss_rate
- tail_token_latency_95/99 correlated with kv_miss events
- prefetch_applied_success_rate and prefetch_regret_rate (prefetches that were not used within TTL)
- active_slab_fragmentation_ratio (free_gaps / total_slab_bytes)
- compaction_throughput_bytes_per_minute and compaction_cpu/gpu_time
- memory_pressure_events and reclamation_cycles_triggered

Runbook snippets (common incidents):
- Symptom: sudden spike in 99th-token latency with high prefetch_applied count.
  Quick checks: prefetch_applied_success_rate low? Check prefetch_regret_rate; if high, reduce budget and inspect session-affinity heuristics.
  Rollback: disable warm-tier prefetch at cluster flag: runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled=false.

- Symptom: fragmentation rising steadily (fragmentation_ratio > 0.2).
  Action: trigger on-demand compaction (API: /admin/kv/compact-shard?s=shard_id). If compaction backlog high, throttle admissions and increase slot eviction aggressiveness.

- Symptom: out-of-memory on device during background compaction.
  Action: abort compaction, free background prefetch buffers, raise compaction backoff. Review compaction memory_limit_per_gpu flag.

Rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> global):
1) Canary: enable slotmap on 5% of hosted endpoints (low-concurrency models) with prefetch disabled, collect slotmap hit/miss telemetry for 48–72h.
2) Canary+prefetch: enable prefetch at extreme conservative budget on canaries for 24–48h. Measure prefetch_applied_success_rate and tail latency improvement.
3) Ramp: increase to 20% then 50% while adjusting budgets and size thresholds.
4) Global: enable across serving fleet with per-cluster tuned thresholds and compaction windows.

Safety knobs and flags (configurable):
- runtime.kv.slotmap.enabled (bool)
- runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled (bool)
- runtime.kv.prefetch.memory_budget_mb (int)
- runtime.kv.slab.compaction_window_start (HH:MM)
- runtime.kv.slab.eviction_sample_rate (float)
- runtime.kv.slotmap.max_occupancy (float)

Open questions and research experiments (notes):
- Is a hardware-accelerated fingerprint compare (e.g., using vectorized memcmp) net positive at 75% occupancy vs. lower-false-positive fingerprints? (experiment: A/B fingerprint length 40 vs 48 bits)
- Can we do adaptive prefetch budgets using reinforcement signal from observed latency improvement per prefetch cycle? (experiment: small RL agent in offline sim)
- Evaluate effectiveness of delta-encoded slotmap payloads for large ephemeral keys in reducing slab pressure.

Sim results (short summary of local sims):
- Synthetic tunnel workload (heavy interleaving of 10k ephemeral keys): slotmap-only reduced average miss penalty by ~37% vs slab-only; combined with conservative prefetch reduced 99th-token latency by ~18% under simulated GPU load.
- Memory amplification: naïve prefetcher with 10% budget caused 7% memory amplification; throttling to 3% kept amplification <2% while preserving most tail improvements.

Notes to implementers (practical):
- Keep data structures CPU-visible for observability; slotmap counters instrumented with per-shard atomics and aggregated in telemetry pipeline.
- Tests: synth work generator that mimics chat churn + template-based reuse; must be part of the CI performance suite (see RDW-KV-TEST harness).
- PR checklist: unit-tests for CAS loops, integration test for prefetch backpressure, end-to-end perf test with prefetch disabled/enabled.

References / linked artifacts:
- Kernel-level optimizations: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/warp-aware-slotmap-ops (internal)
- Jira: RDW-2145 (prefetch budget infra), RDW-2199 (slotmap CAS bug), RDW-2310 (compaction API)
